title: Cinematographic Camera Trajectory Generation in 3D Scenes | EECS at UC Berkeley
content: Cinematographic Camera Trajectory Generation in 3D Scenes | EECS at UC Berkeley Cinematographic Camera Trajectory Generation in 3D Scenes Gina Wu EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2025-198 December 16, 2025 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2025/EECS-2025-198.pdf Language-guided camera trajectory generation in 3D scenes has the potential to revolutionize industries spanning cinematography, virtual production, and robotics, but presents fundamental challenges. While recent advances have enabled new approaches to this problem, significant gaps remain in achieving results that are both technically robust and cinematically compelling. This thesis provides a comprehensive survey of existing state-of-the-art methods and proposes an end-to-end framework for language-guided trajectory generation. We systematically analyze existing methods for cinematographic camera trajectory automation under natural language instructions, categorizing approaches across language understanding, navigation, and generation techniques. Building on this analysis, we propose a unified framework that addresses gaps in current systems. Our framework takes a 3D scene representation and natural language instruction as input, and generates a camera path that prioritizes aesthetic composition, focuses on critical viewpoints, and ensures collision-free natural motion through the environment. Through ablation studies, we identify common failure modes including semantic discontinuities and spatial reasoning challenges, and provide technically-grounded explanations for each. Finally, we identify promising directions for future work. Video results can be found on https://ginazhouhuiwu.github.io/trajectory-generation/.
